Power-creep & lost the plot (lore and gameplay): and now Blackface in a character trailer. I’m done. I’m going to start with the most recent issue: and for context I’ve been playing since 1.0 with no breaks longer than a week over the years. 

HSR has previously faced criticisms of a lack of racial diversity and insensitivity. But Hoyoverse has reached a new low with the new Robin: Summeretto character trailer: “Chasing the Wind” at 0:57-0:58 there’s an explicitly minstrel/blackface caricature. 

I’d love to give the benefit of a doubt and assume “that’s not intentional blackface it’s just an unfortunately similar design choice”

But the why, in the previous scene at 0:56, do none of the light-skinned characters from the same organization, designs meant to mimic each other, not have the red-donut lips. The signature design trait of minstrelsy/blackface.

Hoyoverse needs to fix it and apologize, and better yet, hire some black people for their art and social teams that will stop this kind of insensitive, if not straight up harmful, cultural depictions in their content. 

Moving onto gameplay topics: 
Despite its issues, I’ve enjoyed this game since it was released. But the design of gameplay has steadily decreased for a while. 

New Units are not compatible with old ones, and team building is uninteresting, there very limited choice or variation in what kinds of teams can clear content. 

The powercreep is awful and few characters are lucky to be strong enough to last more than a few patches without vertical investment. 

They no longer have been buffing older characters with NovaFlare, helping them compete, even if only as a worse option, and there hasn’t been a four* character in YEARS. 

And worst of all: there are limited f2p options. You are guaranteed one free 5* weapon/light cone a year, and there are very few 4* options. Even less that are good for characters. 

And on top of ALL of this. There have been very few events as of late, and those events haven’t had a free weapon(light cone) in over a year. 

The female character design especially has gotten strangely bland. I like that old characters have gotten new versions, but so many new characters are the same basic trend of hoyo’s general designs (short frilly dress with no or detached sleeves)

And god forbid any woman gets pants. 

Boss HP inflation (and endgame mechanics that exclude previous teams) gets worse every patch and f2p Artifact farming and reroll tools are so insanely limited. 

Overall, I do not recommend this game until some quality of life priorities start showing. 

While I’d also love the design and story to get better, there’s been some standout quests/characters that would save it otherwise. But considering the slew of other issues I have, it’s just another straw.

Dr. Ratio, my favorite character who debuted in 1.6, has only had one rerun in 3.2.  However, Yao Guang, who debuted only 3 patches ago, already has a rerun?  Make that make sense. Desperate for our money.. As of patch 3.2, the game feels like it’s increasingly desperate for me as a player to spend money. On top of that the game feels as if it’s been dropping in quality every patch since 3.0 started. 

Story telling has taken a noticeable dip in quality from bloated dialogue that’s not engaging to me as a player. On top of that, the amount of black screens with text, which have now been lazily replaced with white screens with black text feel like a lazy and quick way to sum up events instead of creatively showing us happened. 

Drawn out quest lines each patch that take 8 plus hours to complete with no engaging substance to them just feels punishing to play, especially when the game has previously done storytelling much better within a lot less given time.

The game also feels the need to force paywalls down my throat. While I understand the game is free, it doesn’t explain why during the patch where it’s the games second anniversary it’s instead asking me to spend MORE money with events based on paying, enticing me to pull for a new character as soon as I press log in, and making content harder with the best solution being a new shiny character, that’s not even 100% guaranteed. Baring in mind older characters which players like me who have had and enjoyed using for potentially one year or more feel less useable in the current game state with not enough quick response to address/fix it.

For a game that had me hooked all of last year, the last 4 months feel like a slog to play as it feels more prone to unapologetic predatory practices and minimal effort when it comes to game design via balancing and story telling. 

While their are still elements of the game I still enjoy such as team building, and characters themselves being fun to play, especially in certain endgame modes despite power creep getting worse each patch, I still feel my dedication is being punished rather then rewarded. Compared to other games that give us appreciative rewards for dedicated playtime, star rail as of this patch feels desperate to get players to pull and spend money while doing minimal effort to reward us via gameplay. 

I hope positive changes come sooner rather then later because I don’t think I can give the game or devs a years worth of patience to keep playing with a shallow promise of them listening to our feedback to give us minimal returns for our loyalty.

Solved Genshin’s problem(s). As someone who used to play Genshin, for me it had one major flaw and that was grinding. It was incredibly boring to do my daily tasks and use all my resin. However, in HSR, with auto battle and support characters it is so easy to grind materials quickly and efficiently, preventing the burnout that comes with Genshin. 

Not to mention they are much more generous with Stellar jades (primo gems), so I feel like if I stoped playing for a week or even a month I could come back and get enough jades to pull a new character in one update maybe even less.
The content is also a lot less overwhelming. For example the fact that it is not open world. As a perfectionist I always wanted to 100% explore all the areas but it’s near impossible and incredibly frustrating. That’s my issue. Genshin can be soo frustrating, but starrail just works so well around that.

Moving away from Genshin, I love the Sci-Fi aspect and the way that characters wear historical clothing in that context is something I absolutely adore! (Think sparkle, or argenti). The story is entertaining and the characters are sooo well written with consistent personalities. Joke characters like argenti are some of my favourites (hence how I’ve managed to mention him twice) but I really really enjoy the world building too. Super excited to find out what else happens on Penacony, and I’m already looking forward to Pandora! <3

Amazing, perfect after getting bored of Genshin Impact. I started playing Genshin Impact in February 2021 and got to AR 57 but it was honestly a dread to play it sometimes because there was nothing new and the characters didn’t excite me (after scaramouche), I played rarely because I didn’t feel excited anymore. 

Starting out:

BUT I started playing Honkai Star Rail around 20 days ago and got to lv 41 and its AMAZING.
 I felt so nostalgic because of the similar features to Genshin, like it was the same but different which made me experience the whole feel of excitement and novelty again.

Animations: 

HONKAI STAR RAIL ANIMATIONS ARE CREATED BY THE HANDS OF GODS. PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE watch the youtube demos and compare them to genshin ones. Admire the beauty of each ultimate for even 4 stars. 

Lore:

OMG. The story line is so intense and with the addition of the most epic boss fight scenes. (*cough Cocolia boss fight cut scene*)

Wishing / Jades / Characters: 

In HSR, Hoyoverse made it so much easier to get 5 stars even for F2P (e.g Free DR RATIO who is an excellent 5 star Hunt character). Also after certain numbers of pulls on permanent banner, you can get a free 5 star of your choice from the permanent banner (crazy ik). 

I also love how to level up a character it is relatively easy as the domains (calyx and echos ect) are basically always available compared to genshin being a specific day. Also for light cones (eq. to weapons) the materials are the same as for the character leveling up therefore it is SO MUCH EASIER to level up your characters and get really good damage quickly.

Also Hoyoverse is so much more generous with gifting Jades and other things for wishing which is thrilling. 

ALSO, if you want to spend your jades on character banners, no problem, with a bit of time you can grind Simulated Universe and just get free epic 5 star Light cones of your choice. 

There is just so much I can say about this game and I can’t fit onto this review. 

In conclusion, if you are getting bored of Genshin PLEASE TRY HSR because you will feel nostlagia bringing so many great memories.

Story Review. Introduction/Herta Space Station- The start of the game where you learn the mechanics, basic premise, main characters and combat. It’s a basic concept, even if the start is a little underwhelming, they make up with hype moments and funny comedic moments that makes it intriguing.

Jarilo 6/Belobog- An amazing series of stories that all tie together from both the underworld and the over-world side of it. The hype moments are very intense and enticing while also having emotion moments that make you feel things. It does start off slow but makes up for in during the finale

Xianzhou- The first part of it is very interesting but can also leave with a lot of different lore parts that don’t have a conclusion. Having new patches that get added always brings back more hype and a new portion that is interesting to explore. Having intense moments helps keep the less exciting part from being dry. I found it interesting and fun but there are very much mixed opinions about how it’s split up.

Penacony- Made the game 10x more popular because of the beautiful colors and the intense, emotion grabbing story that constantly feels like something bigger will happen. Perfectly wrapped up with complete character development that feels very satisfying.

Amphoreus- The true peak that emotions have during the game. The world building, character development and designs make this whole story feel complete. Grabbing at your heartstrings each patch, it may be long but finally finishing with such a bittersweet ending makes the journey all the more rewarding.

Honest spoiler free review of a day one player. Honkai: Star Rail is technically my first foray into the world of Honkai. You don’t need to have to play the previous reiterations of the title as it is a multi-verse type of game where stories and characters are sometimes nods to the previous games. It is a turn-based game that is more or less story driven. I say that’s because sometimes, it can also be character driven. As of writing this, I am caught up in all the end game content and I’m about two patches behind the main story but everything else is completed. Here are some of the things I want to highlight: 

Gameplay
In terms of game play, as previously mentioned, it is a turned based system. Ultimately the goal is to defeat the enemies within a specific number of turns, for the end game content. I wouldn’t say that there’s a difficulty spike, more like a nice gradual increase if you’re serious about building characters. The game has a character build guide, so if you are the type to not want to think, it’s a pretty solid manual. It literally holds your hand in terms of how to build characters and make teams. I think that’s nice for more casual players but it also gives freeedom for people who like to experiment with their teams and builds. 

Characters 
There is a wide variety of characters. I would say they’re pretty diverse in terms of the tropes they use for characters. The designs are futuristic and unique, they have gorgeous splash art and the in game models are also pretty incredible in terms of details. In terms of merch, if you’re in to that, there is a good verity of characters who get merch so it’s also easy to collect. From a player whose introduction to gacha games back in 2015 is FGO, the ratios of male to female is pretty good, if you care about that sort of thing. You just have to keep in mind that ultimately, the goal of the game is to maintain profit through people paying for their rolls. Do as you want with that statement. 

Overall 
Overall, as a person who plays six gacha games constantly every day, Honkai: Star Rail is a wonderful game. There is an auto function for grinding things, so you really only have to set it and let it run on the side. You really only have to pay attention when doing story, even the end game content could be auto-ed. I don’t really like the direction of the new side game co-op that they’ve introduced. I feel like if you play this game, you’re not really the type to want co-op in your turn based game. 
The story is pretty good, I would say it errs on the typical for gacha in which each big patch is different in quality from the one before. The overarching plot is easy to follow and doesn’t need extra research to understand. 
The experience as a whole is good. Would recommend trying to see for yourself.

Gacha System Feedback. The Gacha System Needs to Be Fixed. The current gacha system is deeply flawed. Having only a 50% chance of getting the character you’ve worked hard and spent time (or money) pulling for is atrocious, especially when the hard pity sits at 80 pulls. That’s an excessive amount of effort for such uncertain results.
This isn’t just a matter of subjective frustration, it’s also objectively unbalanced. The system punishes player dedication instead of rewarding it by a guaranteed that’ll you spend the same amount of your hard-work to get something you should have in the first place. A better approach would be to improve the odds progression after obtaining a guaranteed pull. For example, If a player loses their 50/50, they should still get their guaranteed character next time (as usual). After that guaranteed win, their next banner should have increased odds, say 75/25 up to 100-0 if following streak. Once the player obtains the featured character, the rate resets to 50/50. Additionally, the maximum pity should be reduced from 80 to around 60–70 pulls ( not including the 100-0 ) to make the system objectively more rewarding and respectful of player effort. This isn’t about making the game “too easy” or removing the excitement of chance, it’s about fixing real problems that create player burnout and gambling-like frustration. Games should motivate players, not exploit their patience or emotional investment. Take action before you lose the platform that have made you successful

Veteran player here; ignore older reviews. A lot of the reviews here seem to be coming from people who did not bother to learn Star Rail's combat or those who expect this to be the type of gacha where you are supposed to collect every character.
HSR is a complicated turn-based game, with some of the late-game fights being gruelling to those unprepared. It is also a game that, despite people's complaints, can be beaten using only f2p characters. The game requires you having 8 characters (2 parties of 4) to experience everything it has to offer, including the postgame, and even if you were to never use the gacha a single time or never participate in limited-time events for free characters, the game so far gives you 10 characters, with 1 of those 10 having the ability to change roles in combat over the course of the story.

My biggest advice is take it slow. Only raise the characters you specifically use, make sure your main characters have decent progress with their levels, weapons, relics and traces before increasing Equilibrium (aka the levels your world's enemies are set to). If you see a character you want, make sure to test them out in their trial stage and think about whether or not you actually need them before getting them- the characters do get reruns, so you will always have another chance to get your favourite story characters.

Prioritise getting at least one 'preservation path' (shielding) character besides March 7th. Gepard is the easiest to obtain, but Aventurine is the best. Very few bosses have time limits, so bringing both healers and shielders can help with the most difficult ones.

The gacha is more forgiving than what people claim, with it actually giving better odds even for F2P players than other generally well-liked gachas I've played like Fire Emblem Heroes. As of writing, the devs have just improved the gacha again.

Oh and the story, humor, characters, music, animations and voice acting are all fantastic too. There are quite a few unvoiced parts but for the most part it doesn't take away from the main experience.

Great game I cannot recommend.. I fell in love with Honkai Star Rail(HSR) two years ago, when it was released. I wish that love had remained.

I was initially willing to overlook the monetisation(the Gacha system is essentially a slot machine to unlock DLC characters), due to a compelling story campaign and the promise that anyone, paying or free, could enjoy all the content this game has to offer. Now, as many older characters’ become harder and harder to invest in, and the high level game modes become more and more time consuming — I’m not sure if I want to continue this toxic relationship.

Most players like me still clinging to the game are like bitter ex-es trying to make their former lover improve. HSR demands either your time, or wallet. If you are able to play this game without worrying about the limited events, worrying about logging in daily, or worrying about your roster not having enough damage, then I think HSR is great to play occasionally. Several characters are fun and sweet, and many side quests are genuinely heartbreaking. The combat is also simple enough to understand, but satisfying to optimise.

HSR, currently, suffers from powercreep. Each new character seems stronger than the last — and when each premium character costs either months of saved resources, or $200 worth of premium currency to guarantee, investing into a character, knowing that another playable unit will outrank their damage in three months is harsh.

Aside from premium characters(5 stars), you can also gamble for 4 stars to join your account. There is currently no way to guarantee pulling any 4 star, unless they are gifted through an event. While some of these events are permanent — many are not, and they may not even gift the specific character you wish for. While this might seem minor, the nature of this game’s monetisation as a soft-slot machine makes it entirely possible to spend $250 of currency without pulling a singular copy of a 4 star. While premium characters have a pity system that guarantees a character will eventually be available to you if you spend enough currency — 4 star acquisition relies on hopes and prayers.

These two things mean little if you are able to play this game casually, without spending money/excessive amounts of time — but I would not recommend it for children, students who need to study, or people who might be more inclined to spend money on characters, and people who may become attached to fictional characters easily. Please spend time in nature, with family or with a better game (stardew valley, Elden ring and persona 5 are all games I enjoyed).

Failure to respect the talent this game relies upon continues to be it’s downfall. One of the best things this game has going for it is its high quality voice acting. The cast all bring unparalleled passion to their roles, they are the backbone to the story and emotional experiences that makes this game so fantastic. 

For several months now, many characters in Honkai Star Rail have been muted due to the ongoing voice actors strike. All they are asking for are protections against generative AI, a simple request that will safeguard the future of their industry. The sudden silence from many crucial characters makes cutscenes and intense moments awkward, but that isn’t what’s most disappointing about this situation. 

What is disappointing is that with the simple signing of an interim agreement, every single VA could return to work and provide voices to the characters we adore. But after months, Cognosphere has not done that. Instead, they have left characters silent, and worse, recasted their hard working talent in an act of utter disrespect. 

The decision to sign an interim agreement should be easy, because if Cognosphere chooses to utilise generative AI in their products in any form, they will lose a significant number of customers, including myself. Why would we pay for a product that uses a computer to generate a lacklustre experience, when a human voice actor can do the job 100 times better?

Unless an interim agreement is signed, if Cognosphere continues to disrespect its talent so blatantly, this game is doomed to fail.

Game is good, but lacks in certain aspects.. Honkai: Star Rail is a game I've been playing since it's launch. Prior to it's release, I have been playing Genshin Impact since 1.2 and Honkai Impact 3rd, but lost my account due to problems with the transition to HoyoVerse. 

The turn based combat system is easy to get used to, but ends up being irritating when facing enemies such as Hoolay who have more than 5 turns in one cycle. Characters require an insane amount of grinding to even be usable in the current state of meta and powercreep only gets worse and worse. 

The game has issues with powercreep and hp-inflation. Every enemy nowadays requres too much hp, and even if you have a good character, chances are you'll need their BIS teammates who also happen to be limited characters. In Honkai: Star Rail, if you skip a the banners on just one version, you'll end up falling behind in all endgame content. 

Let's put it like this: Imagine if you got the best character on a lucky pull but you don't have any good teammates for them. You have to wait for their teammates' reruns or for a new character to release that synergise well with them. By the time you have all four teammates (including the first good character you pulled), it's most likely that character has fallen out of meta or become unplayable due to new boss/combat mechanics. 

Free characters are completely unplayable in later stages of the game, forcing players to pull for characters they may not want just for a chance at being able to clear events or certain content. 

The story is amazing and compelling and the worldbuilding is even better. However, transitions from cutscenes into battle are rather choppy and can seem tacky. 

As someone who has been playing since 1.0 and took breaks between patches due to device issues, I couldn't clear any content until I got Firefly on her first banner. Even after getting her, I couldn't make a good team because her best support was locked behind a limited banner and I hadn't progressed far enough to unlock Harmony TB. 

Moving onto 3.0, the game's most recent version, The Herta has definitely made clearing content a lot easier. Creating characters who work well with f2p teammates but even better with limited characters is what I think should be the ideal system of Honkai: Star Rail. Not only does it make things easier for newer or casual players, it also doesn't push an agenda that everyone is a 'must pull', leading to a more enjoyable experience.

In general, the game itself in terms of story, visuals and design is amazing, but the core mechanics of the game and it's content are the issue, such as powercreep and HP inflation.

BEWARE OF GAME - BOTH POSITIVES AND NEGATIVES. Going into this game, I didn’t have a great mindset. I am experienced with HOYO games (genshin, honkai impact) and know that it is very hard to top visually, but the storage consumption, the dialogue and sometimes even hacks and bugs (like deleted weapons etc.) can sometimes be a huge turn off. All my favourite genshin tubers had turned to making Star Rail content and I was determined to try the game and also not like the game.

Going into Honkai Star Rail was a totally different experience for me. The turn based combat and auto battles made it extremely entertaining and unique (for hoyo) and already the events and activities were fun and enjoyable! I soon found myself turning to Honkai Star Rail rather than Genshin.

I’ve been going through some reviews and found people complaining that the game is nothing like genshin, and I need to point out that this is the point! Hoyo should not feel obligated to make copies of genshin all the time, and even though there are similarities, you are able to play Honkai Star Rail in the early phases without feeling the need to play genshin which I think is another great aspect. 

Honkai Star Rail IS a Gacha game, meaning you will either spend lots of money or lots of time grinding for characters that you want, and not playing with event characters will make the game that much more challenging. It is, of course, entirely your take on combat games, and although reading reviews helps, I encourage you to try this game for yourself and take everything into consideration.

That is all. Hope you have a great day.

Extremely good, but know what you’re getting into. It’s a gacha game — getting the best characters requires lots of saving in-game currency, lots of luck, or lots of money. After spending just $15, I’ve gotten enough currency for about 300 warps; already managed to get the current OP destruction character and saving the rest for the next banner; but all I’ve purchased is the slow-drip of 90 gems per day for 30 days, and a battle pass.

The game itself far exceeded my expectations — the graphics, story, voice acting (save for a couple which were completely immersion-breaking — thinking about that guy in the 3rd world which also serves as a random guard in the 2nd world who clearly isn’t cut out to be a VA), and when comparing it to some of the other gacha games I’ve played recently, this one feels the least scummy. They don’t shove in-app purchases in your face, the 5-stars aren’t necessarily required either — they just make the content easier.

Once you’ve finished the campaign it becomes quite grind-y for upgrading your characters and will take several months to get to a full team maxed out, and you’re going to need two teams eventually.
